description:
A worldview-level framing that guides doctrine interpretation.

A paradigm carries no relationship fields: its relationships to directives,
tactics, procedures and other artifacts are authored in the pack's graph
documents (ADR-0064). The retired legacy ``tactic_refs`` / ``paradigm_refs``,
``directive_refs`` and ``references`` fields are rejected.

A paradigm may state its ``principles`` (ADR-0067): one or more core ideas, each a
closed ``{name, description}`` item, in the authored order. A name is unique within
the paradigm, compared ignoring case and surrounding whitespace.

principles.description: The paradigm's core ideas, in the order the author ranks them (ADR-0067). Optional; when present, at least one item. Names are unique within the list, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace (checked by the reader, reported as uniqueItems at the repeated name).
